rule: A US-listed company where AI is a major, publicly stated driver of revenue or capital spending, chosen so the basket covers every layer of the AI supply chain: chips, memory, networking and power, cloud, and software.
note: Frozen at the prereg tag. Never edit this file afterwards; any later basket goes in a new, separately labeled file.

stocks.reason: Most AI models are trained and run on Nvidia's GPUs.
AMD is the main company selling AI chips that compete with Nvidia's.
Broadcom designs custom AI chips for big tech companies and the networking that connects them.
Marvell makes custom AI chips and the optical connections inside data centers.
Micron makes the high-bandwidth memory that AI chips need to work.
Arista builds the network switches that link AI servers together.
Vertiv supplies the power and cooling equipment AI data centers depend on.
Microsoft rents AI computing through Azure, partners with OpenAI, and is one of the biggest AI spenders.
Google builds its own AI models, its own AI chips and an AI cloud.
Amazon's AWS is one of the largest clouds renting out AI computing.
Meta spends heavily on AI to run its ads and build its own models.
Oracle's cloud growth now comes largely from big AI computing contracts.
Palantir sells AI software that companies and governments use to analyze their data.
